title: A study to learn how safe ETHY-001 is and how participants’ body handles it
official: A Randomized, Double-Masked, Placebo-Controlled, Single Ascending Dose Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of ETHY-001.
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the safety and tolerability of ETHY-001
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.The participant is male or female 18 to 65 years of age (Part B), inclusive, at the time of informed consent.
2. 2. The participant has a body mass index of 18 to 32 kg/m2, inclusive (Part A), or ≥18 kg/m2 (Part B) at Screening.
3. 3. The participant agrees to comply with all protocol requirements.
4. 4. The participant is able to provide written informed consent.
5. 5. The participant must agree to defined medications and monitoring as instructed by the site.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Individuals of reproductive potential (all individuals assigned female at birth will be considered of childbearing potential unless they are postmenopausal as confirmed by folliclestimulating hormone levels or surgically sterilized) who do not agree to the contraceptive requirements during the study period and following the last dose of study drug. During this period of protocol-specified contraception requirements, individuals of reproductive potential must also refrain from sperm or egg donation.
2. 10. The participant has 12-lead ECG with clinically significant abnormalities in the opinion of the investigator or with a Fridericia-corrected QT interval (QTcF) >450 msec for males and >470 msec for females at Screening (Parts A and B), Day –1 (Part A), or Day 1 predose (Parts A and B).
3. 11. The participant has a history of alcohol or substance abuse (licit or illicit drugs) within the last 12 months before Screening or considered at high risk of relapse, in the opinion of the investigator.
4. 12. The participant has received an investigational drug within the last 60 days prior to the first dose of study drug, or is in follow-up of another clinical study prior to this study enrollment.
5. 13. The participant has used any prescription or non-prescription drugs (excluding paracetamol >1000 mg/day), antacids, vitamins (other than a daily multivitamin that includes no more than 100 μg selenium and/or 30 μg of biotin), herbal, and dietary supplements (including St John’s Wort) within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to the first dose of study drug, unless in the opinion of the investigator and medical monitor, the medication will not interfere with the study procedures or compromise participant safety.
6. 14. The participant has any of the following laboratory parameter assessments at Screening: a. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) >2 × upper limit of normal (ULN) b. Total bilirubin >1.5 × ULN. Participants with elevated total bilirubin that is secondary to documented Gilbert’s syndrome are eligible if the total bilirubin is <2 × ULN
7. 15. The participant has an estimated glomerular filtration rate of ≤45 mL/min/1.73m2 at Screening (calculation will be based on the race-free Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration formula)
8. 16. The participant has a positive test result for hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C virus antibody, or human immunodeficiency virus types 1 or 2 antibodies at Screening.
9. 17. The participant has tested positive for alcohol and/or drugs of abuse at Screening (Parts A and B) or Day –1 (Part A).
10. 18. The participant is involved in strenuous activity or contact sports within 24 hours before study drug dosing.
11. 19. The participant has donated blood or blood products >450 mL within 30 days before study drug dosing.
12. 2. Breast feeding women. Lactating women may participate in the study if milk is not fed to an infant during the period of protocol-specified contraception requirements.
13. 20. The participant has a history of treatment with teprotumumab or another insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor blocking therapy.
14. 3. The participant has a history of any condition, including but not limited to the following: - cardiovascular event (e.g., stroke, transient ischemic attack, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, coronary artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, or heart failure) - major depressive disorder - inadequately controlled hyperlipidemia - hyponatremia - hypoglycemia - bradycardia
15. 4. The participant has a malignant condition in the past 12 months (except successfully treated basal/squamous cell carcinoma of the skin).
16. 5. The participant has a clinically significant illness, in the opinion of the investigator, within 7 days before the administration of study drug.
17. 6. The participant has other medical conditions or comorbidities which, in the opinion of the investigator, would interfere with study compliance or data interpretation; or, in the opinion of the investigator, taking part in the study would jeopardize the safety of the participant. Individuals with TED and baseline hearing impairment, identified through medical history or audiogram, are eligible to participate in Part B if deemed appropriate by the investigator and if results from recent audiometry testing performed within 3 months prior to Screening are available and documented in the source records.
18. 7. The participant has a history of multiple drug allergies or history of allergic reaction or hypersensitivity to any component of or excipient in study drug.
19. 8. The participant has a history of intolerance to SC injection(s), active skin condition or rash or significant abdominal scarring that could potentially hinder study drug administration or evaluation of local tolerability.
20. 9. The participant has a systolic blood pressure >150 mmHg and/or a diastolic blood pressure >95 mmHg at Screening (Parts A and B), Day –1 (Part A), or Day 1 predose (Parts A and B) that persist after 10 minutes of rest.
